items.stem: Why is hashing a user identifier not sufficient to make a dataset anonymous?

options.text: The same input always hashes to the same value, so records remain linkable and re-identifiable
options.rationale: Correct: deterministic hashes preserve linkage and can be reversed via lookup or combined with quasi-identifiers.
Hashing transforms an identifier; it does not delete data.

options.text: Hashing encrypts all other columns too
options.rationale: Hashing one field does not protect the rest of the record.

options.text: Hashes cannot be stored in a database
options.rationale: Hashes are routinely stored; that is not the issue.

items.explanation: Correct: deterministic hashes preserve linkage and can be reversed via lookup or combined with quasi-identifiers.

items.stem: Which statements about privacy-protective access control are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Least privilege means granting only the access needed for a task
options.rationale: Correct: minimizing standing access reduces exposure of personal data.

options.text: Purpose limitation restricts data use to the reason it was collected
options.rationale: Correct: data accessed for one purpose should not be freely reused for another.

options.text: Broad default access is fine as long as actions are logged
options.rationale: Logging does not substitute for limiting access in the first place.

options.text: Row-level security cannot restrict which records a user sees
options.rationale: Row-level security exists precisely to restrict visible rows.

items.explanation: Correct: minimizing standing access reduces exposure of personal data.; Correct: data accessed for one purpose should not be freely reused for another.

items.stem: What is a quasi-identifier in the context of re-identification risk?

options.text: A field that is not uniquely identifying alone but can identify someone when combined with others
options.rationale: Correct: attributes like ZIP, birth date and gender together can single out individuals.
That is a direct identifier, not a quasi-identifier.

options.text: An encryption key used for masking
options.rationale: A quasi-identifier is data content, not a key.

options.text: A randomly generated token with no meaning
options.rationale: A meaningless token is not a quasi-identifier.

items.explanation: Correct: attributes like ZIP, birth date and gender together can single out individuals.
